column1: # The position table of targets/android.md (rules keyCode, mapKey; also the physical-key mode of androidime): the
# default Android key code per position name, the Linux input scan code of that position, the key code Android's
# generic key layout gives that scan code, and whether the build writes the key or leaves it to the system.
# Sources (read 2026-11-28; names and values only, see CLEAN-ROOM.md "Android"):
#   chromium = Chromium ui/events/keycodes/dom/dom_code_data.inc (BSD-3-Clause), its XKB column (Linux evdev scan
#              code + 8) joined by the W3C code value (the position name), as in targets/xkb-default-keyname.tsv
#   generic  = the key code of that scan code in AOSP frameworks/base data/keyboards/Generic.kl at the tag
#              android-15.0.0_r1 (Apache-2.0), the key layout of every keyboard without a vendor file
#   aosp     = the AOSP keyboard layouts of frameworks/base packages/InputDevices/res/raw (commit 1cdfff555f4a,
#              Apache-2.0): 36 of the 50 give scan code 86 the key code PLUS (`map key 86 PLUS`), because the
#              generic key layout gives 86 and 43 the same key code BACKSLASH
# Columns: position, keyCode (KEYCODE_ name), scanCode (Linux, decimal), generic (the generic key code of scanCode),
# class (character: the build writes the key's block; system: the system keeps the key: modifiers, Enter,
# Backspace, Tab, Escape, navigation, function, media and language keys), source. Positions of
# targets/xkb-default-keyname.tsv without a row: F13 to F24 (Android 15's generic key layout has no key code for
# their scan codes 183 to 194) and BrowserStop (scan code 128, which the generic key layout gives MEDIA_STOP, the key
# code of MediaStop). A row's keyCode differs from generic only for IntlBackslash.
